statement:
A cannery has 76 kg of fruit and 58 L of syrup available today. Its planning sheet reads:
Product | Fruit (kg per batch) | Syrup (L per batch) | Profit (EUR per batch)
Peach jars | 5 | 2 | 43
Pear jars | 3 | 4 | 37
Let x1 be the number of peach batches and x2 the number of pear batches. Both may be fractional and must be nonnegative. Formulate a linear program to maximize total profit.

Transfers from a brewery's fermentation vats are limited to 184 L of water for cleaning and 61 minutes on the transfer line. Each hectolitre of pale ale (x2) uses 11 L of cleaning water and takes 2 minutes to transfer. Each hectolitre of stout (x1) uses 7 L and takes 4 minutes. The brewery earns EUR 125 per hectolitre of stout and EUR 55 per hectolitre of pale ale. The output volumes in hectolitres are nonnegative real numbers. Formulate the profit-maximizing linear program.

A bakery wants the largest total profit from its rye mix (x1) and oat mix (x2), with both outputs measured in kg and allowed to be any nonnegative real numbers. Profit per kg is EUR 4.75 for rye and EUR 6.20 for oat. The flour bin holds 107 kg available for this run. Each kg of rye mix uses 0.8 kg of flour and each kg of oat mix uses 0.65 kg. The packing line can run for at most 176 minutes, at 0.9 minute per kg of rye mix and 1.6 minutes per kg of oat mix. Formulate the linear program.

A print shop plans a run of photo and map prints. Let x1 and x2 be the respective print areas in square metres, both continuous and nonnegative. A customer contract requires at least 22 square metres of combined print area. The usable ink is capped at 2,360 mL. Photos use 125 mL of ink per square metre and maps use 65 mL. The shop earns EUR 28 per square metre of photos and EUR 13 per square metre of maps. Formulate the linear program that maximizes total profit.

A juice press quotes these figures for two products. Each row gives its bottle usage, chilling time and net profit per litre:
Apple juice: 2 bottles, 0.5 minute, EUR 2.30.
Plum juice: 4 bottles, 1.25 minutes, EUR 5.10.
Today's caps are 156 bottles and 60 minutes of chilling. Use x1 for apple litres and x2 for plum litres, with both treated as nonnegative real numbers. Formulate the linear program for maximum total net profit.

A ceramics plant schedules two kinds of slip. Let x1 be litres of white slip and x2 litres of grey slip, both nonnegative and continuous. Processing capacity is 112 minutes and water availability is 82 L. White slip uses 3 minutes and 1 L of water per litre made. Grey slip uses 2 minutes and 2 L of water per litre made. At most 38 L of the two slips combined can be stored. Each litre earns EUR 8 for white and EUR 7 for grey in profit. Formulate the profit-maximizing linear program.

A subcontractor expects EUR 76 profit per metre of copper braid and EUR 49 per metre of aluminium braid. Use x1 for copper metres and x2 for aluminium metres; partial metres are allowed and both quantities must be nonnegative. Orders require at least 19 metres in total. The braider has 94 minutes available, at 5 minutes per metre of copper and 3 minutes per metre of aluminium. Each metre of copper also uses 2 L of coolant and each metre of aluminium uses 3 L. Only 68 L of coolant are available. Formulate the linear program for maximum total profit.

The manager of a fabric dyehouse sent this note for the day's plan: 'Steam is limited to 108 kg and rinse water to 420 L. Do not release less than 16 m of fabric in total. A metre of navy needs 6 kg of steam and 14 L of rinse water and earns EUR 17 in profit. For grey the figures are 3 kg of steam, 25 L of rinse water and EUR 12 in profit.' Let x1 denote metres dyed navy and x2 metres dyed grey. Use continuous nonnegative lengths. Formulate the linear program to maximize total profit.

A milling schedule has three resource limits. Each line below lists the available amount, then the usage per tonne of fine flour, then the usage per tonne of coarse flour.
Mill time (h): 51 | 3.5 | 2.
Electricity (kWh): 289 | 12 | 17.
Bagging time (h): 35 | 1 | 3.
Use x1 for tonnes of fine flour and x2 for tonnes of coarse flour, both continuous and nonnegative. The respective profits are EUR 91 and EUR 74 per tonne. Formulate a linear program to maximize total profit.

A workshop extrusion line earns EUR 32 per metre of wide gasket and EUR 38 per metre of narrow gasket. Let x1 be the wide length and x2 the narrow length in metres, with no requirement to use whole metres and no negative lengths. There are 42 kg of rubber and 134 minutes of machine time. Per metre, wide gasket takes 1.8 kg of rubber and 4 minutes; narrow gasket takes 1.1 kg and 3 minutes. Dispatch can accept up to 31 m across the two widths. Formulate the linear program for maximum total profit.

The nursery buyer needs at least 250 g of nitrogen and 180 g of phosphorus in a purchase of two soluble fertilizers. Per kg, fertilizer West delivers 24 g of nitrogen and 8 g of phosphorus, while fertilizer East delivers 9 g and 21 g respectively. East is priced at EUR 5.40/kg, and West at EUR 16/kg. Let x1 be kg of West and x2 kg of East, both nonnegative and continuous. Formulate the linear program to minimize total purchase cost.

A maintenance depot combines fill fluids A and B. Let x1 and x2 be the litres bought of A and B respectively, with any nonnegative real quantities allowed. The depot needs 40 L or more in total. The mix can contain no more than 260 g of dissolved solids in total; A contributes 9 g/L and B contributes 4 g/L. Buying A costs EUR 2.80/L and buying B costs EUR 3.90/L. Formulate a linear program for the least total cost.

For a greenhouse order the invoice will charge EUR 18 per bag-equivalent of seed mix D (x1) and EUR 25 per bag-equivalent of seed mix W (x2). Partial bag-equivalents cost and contribute proportionally. Each bag-equivalent of D supplies 13 g of fescue seed and 8 g of clover seed. Each bag-equivalent of W supplies 6 g of fescue and 19 g of clover. The order must deliver at least 143 g of fescue and at least 168 g of clover. Quantities are nonnegative. Formulate the linear program to minimize the invoice total.

A glassworks is comparing two bulk inputs. The purchasing quantities are x1 tonnes of cullet and x2 tonnes of virgin mix, both nonnegative real numbers. The charge needs at least 11.7 tonnes of usable glass, from yields of 0.9 tonne per tonne of cullet and 0.78 tonne per tonne of virgin mix. Impurity in the charge must stay at or below 103 kg. Each tonne of cullet brings 14 kg of impurity and each tonne of virgin mix brings 3 kg. The purchase prices are EUR 72 and EUR 156 per tonne, respectively. Formulate the cost-minimizing program.

A feed buyer uses this supplier card:
Field (per kg) | Crumble | Pellets
Digestible protein (g) | 33 | 15
Digestible fibre (g) | 7 | 19
Price (EUR) | 4.25 | 3.80
The delivery must provide at least 290 g of digestible protein and 171 g of digestible fibre. Let x1 be kg of crumble and x2 kg of pellets. Purchases are continuous and nonnegative. Formulate the linear program for the cheapest delivery.

A bakery blends two liquid concentrates for its next run. Choose x1 litres of concentrate R and x2 litres of concentrate S with continuous, nonnegative amounts. The combined volume must reach at least 27 L. The order must provide at least 226 g of active ingredient, with R providing 11 g/L and S providing 5 g/L. It may contain no more than 142 g of sugar from the two concentrates; the sugar contents are 8 g/L for R and 2 g/L for S. R costs EUR 3.20/L and S costs EUR 4.10/L. Formulate the least-cost linear program.

A farm can order two mineral premixes. One kg of premix South costs EUR 7 and supplies 19 g of calcium, 3 g of magnesium and 10 g of phosphorus. The corresponding figures for premix North are EUR 9 per kg, 6 g, 17 g and 8 g. The combined purchase must meet minimums of 173 g of calcium, 147 g of magnesium and 154 g of phosphorus. Let x1 be kg of South and x2 kg of North, with both treated as continuous nonnegative quantities. Formulate the linear program that minimizes the total order cost.

The public works depot needs at least 84 kg of active de-icer in a blend. Let x1 and x2 be the tonnes purchased of grades M and H respectively, where both amounts are nonnegative and continuous. A tonne of M contributes 38 kg of active de-icer and 24 kg of chloride. A tonne of H contributes 27 kg of active de-icer and 9 kg of chloride. The chloride allowance is 46 kg in total. The delivery's mass must fit in a trailer with a capacity of 2.85 tonnes. Prices are EUR 92 per tonne of M and EUR 117 per tonne of H. Formulate the linear program to minimize purchase cost.

A plant is costing a blend from two filter media. In the table the columns give performance and price per kg of medium, and the last row gives the minimum total performance required.
Medium | Water treated (L) | Adsorption capacity (g) | Flow capacity (L/min) | Cost (EUR)
Resin | 23 | 5 | 1.2 | 11.40
Carbon | 14 | 12 | 0.8 | 6.50
Required | 186 | 101 | 10.4 | -
Assume performance is additive and the purchase weights are nonnegative real numbers. Let x1 be kg of resin and x2 kg of carbon. Formulate the program for the lowest total cost.

A soap maker's total purchase cost is based on EUR 8.50 per kg of base oil L and EUR 12.70 per kg of base oil T. The blend must supply at least 8.4 kg of fatty acids and at least 5.1 kg of saturated fatty acids. Every kg of L supplies 0.68 kg of fatty acids, including 0.24 kg of saturated fatty acids. Every kg of T supplies 0.79 kg of fatty acids, including 0.57 kg of saturated fatty acids. The blending tank can hold at most 11.5 kg of oil. Let x1 be kg of L and x2 kg of T, with both amounts continuous and nonnegative. Formulate the cost-minimizing program.
